2. The facts revealed in the leave petition, in short, are that Sub-inspector Nasir Ahmed attached to Mirpur Police Station during 1996 took accused petitioner on remand in connection with Mirpur P.S. Case No.6 dated 15.08.1996 under Sections 395/397 of the Penal Code and during interrogation the accused petitioner admitted to have in his possession a shutter gun with ammunition kept in his residential house and then he was taken to his house and he himself brought out the arms and ammunition and so a case was started against him under Section 19A and 19(f) of the Arms Act being Mirpur P.S. Case No.6 dated 26.11.1996. The case being investigated charge sheet was submitted against the 'accused petitioner accordingly. During trial the accused petitioner was released on bail, but he absconded. Be that as it may, prosecution produced five witnesses while none was examined on behalf of the defence. Additional Session. Judge, 2nd Court and Special Tribunal No.3, Kushtia in consideration of the evidence on record convicted the accused petitioner under Section 19A and 19(f) of the Arm. Act read with Section 26 of the Special Powers Act, 1974 and sentenced him to suffer imprisonment for 14 (fourteen) years and to pay fine of Tk.5, 000/- (five thousand), in default, to suffer rigorous imprisonment for 6 (six) months more. The accused petitioner being in abscondence did not file any appeal. After expiry of the statutory period of limitation for filing appeal, he filed Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.6453 of 2000 before the High Court Division tinder Section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure. The said application was rejected summarily by the High Court Division on 23 October 2000. Thereafter, he moved the High Court Division m Writ Petition No.2067 of 2002 and the High Court Division by impugned judgment and order discharged the rule. Hence is this petition. 

 3. In support of the petition Mr. M. A. Aziz Khan, learned Advocate submits, inter alia, that this is a case of no evidence and as such the High Court Division committed error in discharging the rule. Referring to Section 27(6) of the Special Powers Act, the learned Advocate submits that the Special Tribunal had no jurisdiction to try the petitioner in his absence without complying with the requirement of Section 27(6) of the Special Powers Act. He, therefore, submits that it is a fit case for interference by the High Court Division and thus the impugned judgment calls for interference. 

 4. We have considered the submissions and perused the materials on record. It appears that P.W.1 Nasir Ahmed, sub-inspector of -police in his deposition clearly stated that during interrogation while was on remand the accused petitioner admitted possession of the arms and the ammunition and himself produced the same from his homestead and so the said arms and ammunition were seized by him and accordingly the case was started. Though the witness was put to cross-examination but no material contradiction could be elicited from his evidence. P.W.2 Md. Sowruar Uddin Sheikh, Sub-inspector of police accompanied P.W. 1 Nasir Ahmed during the search. He in his evidence corroborated P.W.I in all material points. Nothing beneficial to the petitioner could be brought out from the cross-examination. P.W.3 Md. Habibur Rahman, P.W.4 Nurul Amin and P.W.5 Moteher Hossein, seizure list witnesses corroborated in their evidence P.Ws I and 2, In view of cogent evidence of the witnesses it cannot be said that this is a case of no evidence. The submission of the learned Counsel, on this score, therefore, has got no substance. 

 (6A) Where in a case after the production or appearance of an accused person before the Tribunal or his release on bail, the accused person absconds or fails to appear before it, the procedure as laid down in subsection (6) shall not apply and the Tribunal shall, after recording its decision so to do, try such person in his absence. 

 On perusal of the aforesaid provision of law it appears that in case , of trial of an absconding accused no doubt it is necessary to publish a direction for his appearance before the court in at least two Bengali newspapers having wide circulation and it is correct to say that in the instant case no such step was taken. But on perusal of Sub-section (6A) mentioned above it appears that in case of non-appearance of an accused-in course of his trial after his release on bail the procedure as laid down in Sub-section (6) has got no application. In such clear indication of law we are of the view that there was no necessity to adopt to the procedure mentioned in Sub-section (6) of Section 27 in the instant case, inasmuch as the accused petitioner was allowed bail during trial and thereafter he remained absent. This submission of the learned Counsel also thus is found to be deviod of any substance.
